speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a pruritic rash on your trunk and extremities along with a recent low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. To help narrow this down, have you had any close contact with anyone who had chickenpox, measles, or shingles recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: The patient is an 11-year-old with a rash that appeared after a week of flu-like symptoms (fever, rhinorrhea, headache) and notably spares the perioral area. Given the sequence of events and the facial rash distribution, do you recall any recent exposure to a child with measles or rubella?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Rubella (German Measles). The clinical presentation of a rash starting on the face and spreading to the trunk, sparing the perioral area, following a prodrome of fever and rhinorrhea is classic for rubella in an 11-year-old.
